text: The Irish economy continued to grow strongly, supported by modified domestic demand and MNEs’ exports. Real GNI* grew by about 4 percent in 2025 after 4.8 percent in 2024, while real GDP rose 12.3 percent in 2025 before contracting 17 percent (y-o-y) in 2026 Q1. Headline HICP inflation averaged 2.1 percent in 2025, reaching 3.6 percent in March 2026. Fiscal surplus reached 1.8 percent of GDP (3.3 percent of GNI*). The 2025 fiscal stance is assessed to be moderately expansionary, while the external position is preliminarily assessed to be moderately stronger than medium-term fundamentals.
